statement: Given that 2^10 = 1024, how many digits does the number 2^100 have?

choices.misconception: I used 2^10 as about 10^3 to get 2^100 as about 10^30, and thought 10^30 has 30 digits, but it has 31.
I used the rougher estimate 2^3 as about 10, which makes 2^100 about 10^33.3 and suggests 34 digits, but 2^3 is only 8.
I thought each doubling adds half a digit, so 100 doublings make 50 digits.
I thought each doubling adds one digit, so 100 doublings make 100 digits.

hints: 2^100 = 1024^10 = 1.024^10 x 10^30. Decide roughly how big 1.024^10 is, and remember how many digits a power of 10 has.
1.024^10 is about 1.27: more than 1 and far less than 10. So 2^100 is between 10^30 and 10^31.

solutions.reliable: 2^100 = (2^10)^10 = 1024^10 = 1.024^10 x 10^30. The factor 1.024^10 is about 1.27, roughly 1 + 10 x 0.024 plus a little, so it is more than 1 and certainly less than 10. Hence 2^100 lies between 10^30 and 10^31. Every number from 10^30 up to just below 10^31 has 31 digits, so 2^100 has 31 digits. The transferable idea: estimate a huge power as a power of ten times a factor you can bound, and remember that 10^k has k + 1 digits.
solutions.elegant: Since log 2 is about 0.301, 2^100 is about 10^30.1, and the number of digits is the whole-number part of 30.1 plus one: 31.

whyOnTest: Counting the digits of a huge power is an estimation task, and the classic slips are the off-by-one in the digits of 10^k and an estimate that is too rough.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
